input.quote: Kubient hereby grants to Customer a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable license to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient
input.rationale: The only licence grant (paragraph 2) runs to "Customer" alone, with no mention of AP affiliates or contractors acting on our behalf and no mechanism to add them, and it is expressly "revocable" with no qualification — revocation is not tied to termination or uncured breach, so Kubient could pull platform access at will (paragraph 21 separately revokes the licence on termination, but does not limit revocation to that event). That fails even the fallback (affiliates covered on notice), and at-will revocability sits in walk-away territory. The general assignment provision (p0072) permits assignment of the Agreement to an affiliate or M&A successor, which partly addresses transaction continuity, but the grant itself is "non-transferable, non-assignable". Redline extends the grant to affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, confirms successor transferability, and limits revocation to expiration or termination under paragraph 4. Scope limits on use of the platform are left to the IP review to avoid double-flagging.

proposal.summary: Extend licence grant to AP affiliates and contractors, allow successor transfer, and remove at-will revocability
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the Auction Platform licence to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, confirmed it transfers to a successor in an M&A transaction, and tied revocation to termination of the Agreement rather than Kubient's discretion. Our playbook does not permit a licence that is revocable at will or that excludes affiliates and contractors with no path to add them.
